attribution.note: Marcus directly asserts that the opposition crosses party lines.

semantics.note: The proposition captures his observation about opposition across parties; the referenced poll supplies the local-construction scope.

contract.note: Substantial opposition in both major parties is an ordinary reading. The contract appropriately avoids requiring equal opposition or unanimity.

evidence.note: The Annenberg-attributed reproduction predates the cutoff and reports the relevant survey: opposition is 69% among Democrats, 54% among Republicans and 53% among independents.

reviews.rationale: The same local-construction question shows substantial opposition across both major parties and independents. Differences between parties do not undermine the claim. No material counterevidence is supplied.

attribution.note: Marcus directly asserts that opposition is rising fast and identifies the Annenberg poll as his source.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the asserted trend and its poll-based qualifier. This describes an observed change, not a forecast.

contract.note: A substantial increase over a few months is an ordinary reading of the claim. The local scope and comparison period follow the referenced survey.

evidence.note: The original report predates the cutoff and compares weighted opposition across the relevant waves. It reports an 11.8-point increase, with a 95% interval of +6.9 to +16.6; the within-person check agrees.

reviews.rationale: Opposition increased from 48.9% to 60.6% over roughly four months. The reported change is substantial and its confidence interval excludes zero. The within-person analysis reinforces the finding; stable attitudes on other AI questions measure different outcomes.
